verses.text: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
Early the next morning, he came back to the temple. All the people gathered around him, and he sat down to teach them.
The legal experts and Pharisees brought in a woman caught committing adultery. They made her stand right there in the middle.
They said to him, “Teacher, we caught this woman in the act of adultery.
Moses commanded us in the Law to stone women like this. So, what do you say?”
They were setting him up, hoping to get something they could use to accuse him. Jesus bent down and started writing on the ground with his finger.
They kept pressing him with questions. He stood up and said, “Let the one among you who has never sinned throw the first stone at her.”
Then he bent down again and kept writing on the ground.
When they heard that, their conscience hit them. One by one, starting with the oldest, they walked away. Jesus was left there alone with the woman still standing in the middle.
Jesus stood up and asked her, “Woman, where did they go? Did nobody condemn you?”
She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus told her, “I don’t condemn you either. Go, and from now on, don’t sin anymore.”
Jesus spoke to them again: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me won’t walk around in darkness; they’ll have the light that gives life. 💡
The Pharisees challenged him: “You’re speaking for yourself. That testimony doesn’t count.”
Jesus answered, “Even if I speak for myself, my testimony is true. I know where I came from and where I’m going. You don’t know where I came from or where I’m going.
You judge by human standards. I don’t judge anyone.
And even when I do judge, my judgment is true, because I’m not alone. The Father who sent me is with me.
Your own Law says that the testimony of two people counts as valid.
I testify about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”
They asked him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered, “You don’t know me or my Father. If you knew me, you’d know my Father too.”
Jesus said these things while teaching in the temple treasury. Still, nobody arrested him, because his time hadn’t come yet.
Jesus told them again, “I’m going away. You’ll look for me, but you’ll die in your sins. You can’t come where I’m going.”
The Jewish leaders said, “Is he going to kill himself? Is that what he means by, ‘You can’t come where I’m going’?”
He told them, “You come from below; I come from above. You belong to this world; I don’t belong to this world.
I told you that you will die in your sins. Unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.
They asked him, “Who are you, then?” Jesus answered, “I’ve been telling you from the start.
I have plenty to say about you and plenty to judge. But the One who sent me is true, and I’m telling the world what I heard from him.”
They didn’t realize he was talking to them about the Father.
So Jesus said, “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you’ll know that I AM. I do nothing on my own; I say what the Father taught me.
The One who sent me is with me. The Father hasn’t left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”
While he was saying these things, many people believed in him.
Jesus said to the people who had believed him, “If you stay with my word, you’re really my disciples.
You’ll know the truth, and the truth will set you free.” 🔓
They answered, “We’re Abraham’s descendants. We’ve never been anybody’s slaves. So how can you say, ‘You’ll be set free’?”
Jesus answered, “I’m telling you the truth: everyone who keeps sinning is sin’s slave.
A slave doesn’t stay in the family home forever, but a son belongs there forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you’ll be free for real.
I know you’re Abraham’s descendants, but you’re trying to kill me because my word has no room in you.
I tell you what I have seen with my Father. But you are doing what you have seen with your father.”
They replied, “Abraham is our father.” Jesus said, “If you were Abraham’s children, you’d do what Abraham did.
But now you’re trying to kill me—a man who told you the truth I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do that.
You’re doing what your father does.” They said, “We weren’t born through sexual immorality. We have one Father: God.”
Jesus told them, “If God were your Father, you’d love me, because I came from God and I’m here. I didn’t come on my own; he sent me.
Why can’t you understand what I’m saying? It’s because you can’t bear to hear my word.

Your father is the devil, and you want to do what your father desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks from his own nature: he is a liar and the father of lies.
But because I tell you the truth, you don’t believe me.
Which one of you can prove I’ve sinned? If I’m telling the truth, why don’t you believe me?
Whoever belongs to God hears God’s words. That’s why you don’t hear: you don’t belong to God.”
The Jewish leaders answered him, “Aren’t we right to say you’re a Samaritan and have a demon?”
Jesus replied, “I don’t have a demon. I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
I am not chasing my own glory. There is One who seeks and judges.
I’m telling you the truth: whoever keeps my word will never see death.”
The Jewish leaders said, “Now we know you have a demon! Abraham died, and so did the prophets, but you say, ‘Whoever keeps my word will never taste death.’
Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died too. Who do you think you are?”
Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, that glory is nothing. My Father is the one who glorifies me—the very one you claim as your God.
You don’t know him, but I do. If I said I didn’t know him, I’d be a liar like you. But I do know him, and I keep his word.
Your father Abraham was thrilled to see my day. He saw it and was glad.”
The Jewish leaders said to him, “You aren’t even fifty years old, and you’ve seen Abraham?”
Jesus said, “I’m telling you the truth: before Abraham came into being, I AM.”
So they picked up stones to throw at him. But Jesus slipped away and left the temple, passing right through the middle of them.
